title: Why I Choose TypeScript for Every New Project
excerpt: After years of JavaScript, TypeScript transformed how I ship reliable production code. Here's the pragmatic case for adopting it.
content:
TypeScript isn't just about types — it's about confidence. When you refactor a large codebase, the compiler becomes your co-pilot. When you onboard a new developer, the types become your documentation.

Over the last four years, I've shipped TypeScript across fintech, logistics, and SaaS products. The pattern is consistent: fewer runtime bugs, faster onboarding, and a codebase that scales without fear.

## The Real Value Is DX

Developer experience is a product metric. When your team moves faster with fewer bugs, you ship more value. TypeScript's autocomplete, refactoring safety, and inline errors pay dividends on every sprint.

## When to Skip It

Small scripts, rapid prototypes, or solo weekend projects don't always need the overhead. But for anything that lives beyond a week in production — TypeScript is always worth it.

## Getting Started

Start with `strict: false`, enable rules incrementally. Don't let the config intimidate you. The migration can be gradual, and every file you convert is a win.

title: The Anatomy of a Great API Contract
excerpt: A well-designed API contract is the difference between a system that scales and one that becomes technical debt overnight.
content:
API design is product design. Every endpoint you expose is a commitment — to your consumers, your team, and your future self.

The best APIs I've worked with share three things: predictability, versioning from day one, and error messages that actually help.

## Predictability

Use consistent naming, consistent response shapes, and consistent error formats. If `GET /users` returns `{ data: [] }`, then `GET /posts` should too.

## Version Early

Add `/v1/` to your base path before you ship anything. You'll thank yourself when a breaking change becomes necessary six months later.

## Error Messages Are UX

A `400 Bad Request` with no body is useless. A `400` with `{ error: 'email_invalid', field: 'email', message: 'Must be a valid email address' }` is actionable. Your API consumers are developers — treat them with respect.

title: Freelancing as a Developer: Year One Lessons
excerpt: What I wish I knew before going independent. On pricing, clients, contracts, and staying sane.
content:
The first year of freelancing is humbling. You learn that technical skill is table stakes — communication, pricing, and expectations management are what separate sustainable freelancers from burned-out ones.

## Charge More Than You Think

Your day rate should account for: taxes, benefits you no longer get, unpaid admin time, gaps between contracts, and the value you deliver (not just the hours you bill). Double your instinct. Then add 20%.

## Contracts Protect Everyone

A clear statement of work prevents scope creep, misalignment, and awkward conversations. It's not about distrust — it's about clarity.

## Choose Clients Like Employees Choose Employers

You have more leverage than you think. A client who respects your time and trusts your judgment is worth far more than one paying 20% more but micromanaging every commit.

## Communication Is the Product

Weekly updates, clear milestone reports, honest timelines. Your clients aren't just paying for code — they're paying to sleep well knowing their project is in good hands.

title: Building for Performance: A Practical Checklist
excerpt: Performance isn't a feature — it's a baseline. A no-nonsense checklist for web apps that load fast and stay fast.
content:
Every millisecond of load time costs conversions. Studies are consistent: sub-1s loads drive measurably higher engagement. Here's my go-to checklist before any production deploy.

## Images

- Use WebP or AVIF formats
- Lazy-load everything below the fold
- Set explicit width/height to prevent layout shift
- Use CDN delivery with aggressive cache headers

## JavaScript

- Code-split by route
- Defer non-critical scripts
- Audit your bundle with `vite-bundle-visualizer`
- Remove unused dependencies ruthlessly

## CSS

- Inline critical CSS for above-the-fold content
- Avoid render-blocking stylesheets
- Use CSS animations over JS animations where possible

## Network

- Enable Brotli compression
- Use HTTP/2 or HTTP/3
- Prefetch next routes on hover
- Cache API responses aggressively with proper invalidation
